title: Isolation, expansion and characterization of porcine urinary bladder smooth muscle cells
author: Pokrywczynska, Balcerczyk, et al.
materials: In order to confirm removal of the mucosa/submucosa and serosa, the fragments of the smooth muscle layer (1 cm2) were fixed for 48 h in 10 % buffered formalin, embedded in paraffin, sectioned at 4 μm tick sections and stained routinely with hematoxylin and eosin. To identify urothelial cells, immunohistochemical staining with monoclonal antibody against the p63 protein (dilution of the manufacturer, Roche, Germany) was performed. Presence of the smooth muscle cells was confirmed using a mouse monoclonal antibody against α-smooth muscle actin (anti- alpha smooth muscle actin [1A4] antibody, dilution of the manufacturer, Abcam, UK). Antigen- primary antibody complexes were visualized by use of a secondary antibody conjugated to horseradish peroxidase (EnVisionTM FLEX anti Mouse/Rabit HRP; Dako, Denmark).

Isolated cells were seeded at a density of 2 × 104 cells/cm2. Three different growth media were compared. Two media (A and B) consisted of DMEM HG supplemented with 100U/ml penicillin, 100 μg/ml streptomycin, 5 μg/ml amphotericin B, 100 μg/ml gentamycin and one of the two sera: 10 % FBS Good (Medium A; Pan-Biotech, Germany) or FBS Sigma (Medium B; Sigma, Germany). Third medium was a Smooth muscle Growth Medium, SmGM-2 (Medium C; Lonza. Germany). Cells were cultured at 37 °C in 5 CO2 and 95 % humidity. Growth medium was changed every 2–3 days. Cell morphology and growth were evaluated under inverted light microscope.

To analyze the phenotype of cells in primary cultures immunofluorescent staining of anti- alpha smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) and anti- smoothelin were performed. Isolated cells were seeded into 24-well cell culture plate with glass coverslips. In the 5th day after the establishment of the primary culture, cells were fixed by 15 min. incubation in 2 % paraformaldehyde (Sigma, Germany). Non-specific antibody binding sites were blocked by incubation with 1 % bovine serum albumin (BSA, Sigma, Germany) in PBS. As primary antibodies murine monoclonal anti- α-smooth muscle actin antibody (dilution 1:100, anti-alpha smooth muscle actin [1A4] antibody, Abcam, UK,) and murine monoclonal anti-smoothelin antibody (dilution 1:100, Anti-Smoothelin antibody [R4A], Abcam, UK) were used. Cultures were incubated with primary antibodies for 1.5 h. Thereafter, cells were incubated (room temperature, 1 h) with the secondary antibody conjugated with a fluorescent dye (dilution 1:100, anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488, Life Technologies, Germany). Nuclei were stained by 10 min. incubation with DAPI (dilution 1:20.000, Sigma, Germany). After washing with PBS, mounting medium Aqua-Poly/Mount (Polysciences, Inc., USA) was applied. Microscopic slides were analyzed using a confocal microscope (Nikon Eclipse Ti-U, Japan).

Cell growth was monitored also in real time using the X-Celligence system (Roche, Germany). Cells were seeded on 16- well plate (14 examined, two controls) (E- Plate 16, Roche, Germany) at a density of 2 × 104cells/cm2. X-Celligence system base on a measurement of the impedance (changes in electrical resistance) of adherent cells via biosensors placed on the bottom of each well of the plate. Impedance is then processed to Cell Index. Measurements were made every 30 min. for a period of 7 days. Cell growth curve was plotted as a dependence of Cell Index from the time of culture.

Data for success rate of establishment of primary cultures of porcine urinary bladder smooth muscle cells were presented in Table 2. All primary cultures established in medium C (SmGM-2) showed normal morphology, and increase in number of cells which allowed to reach confluence. Success rate of cultures grown in medium C regardless of method of isolation was 100% (36/36 cultures). In the case of all cultures established in medium B (DMEM HG, FBS Sigma) cells showed normal morphology, but common cell detachments have not allowed to reach a confluency, and consequently the success rate was 0%. Cultures established in medium A (DMEM HG, FBS Pan-Biotech) were characterized by changes in cellular morphology and inhibition of cell proliferation. However, slightly better cell adhesion compared to medium B allowed to achieve a confluency with normal morphology in 2 from 45 cultures (Table 2). Establishment of primary cultures of UB- SMCs using the explant technique was the least effective, and reproducible among the compared methods. Most of the tissue fragments detached from the surface of culture dish during the first days of culture, while the attached explants not always lead to cells spreading. Finally, none of the explants cultures was successful. steps.title: Harvest and mince smooth muscle tissue
steps.instruction: Obtain porcine urinary bladder, surgically remove mucosa/submucosa and serosa, then cut the smooth muscle layer into fragments of approximately 1 cm². Mince each fragment into ~1 mm² pieces.

steps.title: Isolate SMCs using chosen method
steps.instruction: Perform one of the five isolation protocols (Methods I‑V) as described, using the specified enzymes, volumes, concentrations, and incubation times.

substeps.instruction: Method I (Collagenase II + Dispase II): Prepare 40 mL digestion solution containing Collagenase II (0.15 % w/v, ≈275 U/mg), Dispase II (0.2 % w/v, ≈175 U/mg), CaCl₂ 5 mM in HBSS. Add minced tissue, incubate 1.5 h at 37 °C. Neutralize with an equal volume of DMEM High‑glucose medium containing 10 % FBS.

Method II (Collagenase II + Trypsin): Prepare 5 mL digestion solution containing Collagenase II (0.15 % w/v, ≈275 U/mg), Trypsin‑EDTA (0.25 % v/v), CaCl₂ 5 mM in HBSS. Incubate tissue for 1 h at 37 °C. Neutralize with equal volume of DMEM High‑glucose + 10 % FBS.

Method III (Collagenase II only): Prepare 5 mL digestion solution containing Collagenase II (0.15 % w/v, ≈275 U/mg) and CaCl₂ 5 mM in HBSS. Incubate tissue for 16 h at 37 °C. Neutralize with equal volume of DMEM High‑glucose + 10 % FBS.

Method IV (Trypsin → Collagenase II): Incubate tissue fragments in Trypsin (0.25 % v/v) for 30 min (room temperature or 37 °C). Transfer fragments to a Petri dish, gently scrape with the blunt side of a scalpel to remove residual mucosa/submucosa/serosa, then mince. Add 5 mL Collagenase II (0.15 % w/v, ≈275 U/mg) with CaCl₂ 5 mM and incubate 1 h at 37 °C. Stop digestion by adding an equal volume of DMEM High‑glucose + 10 % FBS.

Method V (Explant): Place minced tissue pieces onto the bottom of a 60 mm culture dish. Leave the dish open in a laminar‑flow cabinet for 10–15 min to allow tissue to adhere. Add culture medium carefully so fragments remain attached. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Change medium on day 3 and remove detached fragments; thereafter change medium every 2–3 days until confluent colonies form.

steps.title: Filter and centrifuge cell suspension
steps.instruction: For Methods I‑III, filter the neutralized suspension through a 100 µm nylon cell strainer (BD, USA) and centrifuge at 1500 × g for 5 min. For Method IV, centrifuge the suspension at 250 × g for 2 min, collect the supernatant, resuspend the pellet, repeat at 150 × g for 2 min, discard undigested tissue, pool supernatants, then centrifuge the pooled suspension at 1500 × g for 5 min. Discard supernatant and resuspend the final pellet in the appropriate growth medium.

steps.title: Count viable cells
steps.instruction: Determine cell number and viability using the trypan blue exclusion assay.

steps.title: Seed cells in selected growth medium
steps.instruction: Plate isolated cells at a density of 2 × 10⁴ cells/cm² in one of three media: (A) DMEM High‑glucose + 10 % FBS (Pan‑Biotech) + 100 U/mL penicillin, 100 µg/mL streptomycin, 5 µg/mL amphotericin B, 100 µg/mL gentamicin; (B) same formulation with FBS Sigma; or (C) SmGM‑2 (Lonza).

steps.title: Maintain primary culture
steps.instruction: Incubate cultures at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 95 % humidity. Replace growth medium every 2–3 days and monitor cell morphology with an inverted light microscope.

steps.title: Verify tissue removal by histology/IHC
steps.instruction: Fix smooth‑muscle fragments (1 cm²) in 10 % buffered formalin for 48 h, embed in paraffin, cut 4 µm sections, and stain with hematoxylin‑eosin. Perform immunohistochemistry using monoclonal anti‑p63 (manufacturer’s dilution, Roche) to detect urothelium and anti‑α‑SMA (1A4, manufacturer’s dilution, Abcam) to detect smooth muscle. Visualize with EnVision™ FLEX anti‑Mouse/Rabbit HRP (Dako).

steps.title: Immunofluorescence staining of cultured cells
steps.instruction: Seed cells onto glass‑coverslip‑bearing 24‑well plates. On day 5, fix with 2 % paraformaldehyde for 15 min, block with 1 % BSA in PBS, then incubate with primary antibodies (mouse anti‑α‑SMA, 1:100; mouse anti‑smoothelin, 1:100) for 1.5 h at room temperature. Wash, incubate with Alexa Fluor 488‑conjugated anti‑mouse secondary (1:100) for 1 h at room temperature, wash, stain nuclei with DAPI (1:20 000) for 10 min, wash, mount with Aqua‑Poly/Mount, and image using a confocal microscope (Nikon Eclipse Ti‑U).

steps.title: Measure fluorescence intensity
steps.instruction: Using EZ‑C1 3.90 FreeViewer (Nikon), measure cell surface area (µm²), cell fluorescence intensity, and background intensity. Calculate relative cell fluorescence (RCF) as RCF = (cs × fic) − (cs × fib).

steps.title: Flow cytometry analysis of α‑SMA
steps.instruction: Harvest ~0.5 × 10⁶ cells (method I, cultured in SmGM‑2), wash twice with PBS, centrifuge 5 min at 700 × g, resuspend in 200 µL staining buffer (2 % FBS, 0.09 % sodium azide). Add α‑SMA‑PE antibody (1 µL per 1 mL cells) and isotype control (4 µL per 1 mL cells). Incubate 30 min in the dark at 4 °C, wash twice with staining buffer, and analyze on a FACSCanto II flow cytometer.

steps.title: Monitor proliferation with X‑Celligence
steps.instruction: Seed cells onto an E‑Plate 16 (Roche) at 2 × 10⁴ cells/cm² (14 test wells, 2 controls). Record impedance‑derived Cell Index every 30 min for 7 days using the X‑Celligence system; plot Cell Index versus time to generate growth curves.
